before.title: Transformation of tensor, covector, derivative and current components under affine Lorentz maps
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is the affine map x'(p) = Lambda x(p) + b with linear part Lambda (a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz), and let Omega be an open subset of A. Let J: Omega -> V, k, and T be a C^k vector field, a C^k covector field and a C^k type-(r,s) tensor field on Omega in the sense of def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, with components J^a, k_a and T^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} in the chart x, and primed components in the chart x'. Then: (i) J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b: a contravariant index gains the factor Lambda^a_b, i.e. components transform by multiplication with the transition matrix. (ii) k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b: a covariant index gains the factor (Lambda^{-1})^b_a. If theta(p) = k_a x^a(p) + theta_0 is an affine scalar function with constant covector k and constant theta_0, then theta(p) = k'_a x'^a(p) + theta'_0 with k' as above and theta'_0 := theta_0 - k'_a b^a, so the phase function is invariant when the constant term is transformed together with the covector. (iii) T'^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} = Lambda^{a_1}_{c_1} ... Lambda^{a_r}_{c_r} (Lambda^{-1})^{d_1}_{b_1} ... (Lambda^{-1})^{d_s}_{b_s} T^{c_1...c_r}_{d_1...d_s}: every contravariant index gains a factor Lambda and every covariant index a factor Lambda^{-1}, and the law is consistent with the multilinear evaluation of T(p) after substituting the transformed basis. Every contraction of one contravariant with one covariant index is invariant, and the metric components satisfy eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab}. (iv) The coordinate partial derivatives satisfy partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b wherever the derivatives exist. Consequently the divergence of a vector field is invariant, partial'_a J'^a = partial_a J^a, and for a C^1 type-(2,0) field T one has partial'_a T'^{ab} = Lambda^b_c partial_a T^{ac}. (v) Alternating covariant tensor fields transform by the covariant law on each slot; the oriented volume form of the model satisfies epsilon'_{abcd} = epsilon_{abcd}, since det Lambda = +1, whereas a general Lorentz matrix with det = -1 changes its sign. (vi) Let J be a C^1 vector field with components (J^0,J^1,J^2,J^3) in an inertial chart, and write the spatial block as J_cov := (J^1,J^2,J^3) and denote by partial_i the spatial partial derivatives in the chart. Then the continuity equation partial_a J^a = 0 is equivalent to partial_0 J^0 + sum_i partial_i J^i = 0, and under the passive boost with parameter beta (Lambda = B(beta), Lambda^{-1} = B(-beta)) the components transform as J'^0 = gamma(J^0 - beta . J_cov), J'_cov = J_cov + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . J_cov) beta - gamma beta J^0. (vii) If U is a C^1 future timelike vector field and rho_0 a C^1 scalar field, then J := rho_0 U is a C^1 vector field and its first component satisfies J^0 = rho_0 U^0; writing rho := J^0 (the coordinate density in the chart) and u := U/U^0 (the coordinate velocity), one has rho = rho_0 u^0. Coordinate density and the scalar multiplier rho_0 are different objects: they agree only in charts in which u^0 = 1. Interpretation boundary: the identification of a physical charge-current with a vector field, and of rho with a measured charge density, is a model premise of the electromagnetic framework; this item is a statement about the transformation of components of specified fields and does not by itself assert that any physical current transforms as a vector.
before.strategy: Proof plan. (i) and (ii) are the definitions of components: for a vector field, J'(p) = sum_a J'^a(p) partial'_a|_p and partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b, so comparing coefficients with J = sum_b J^b partial_b gives J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b; the covector transform is the dual statement k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b. The affine phase invariance in (ii) is the displayed substitution k_a x^a = k'_c x'^c - k'_c b^c. (iii) is the multilinear evaluation: writing T(p) on the transformed basis and using the definition of the components, each contravariant slot contributes Lambda and each covariant slot the inverse; the contraction claim follows from (Lambda^{-1})^a_b Lambda^b_c = delta^a_c, and eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab} is the matrix form of the defining Lorentz property of Lambda. (iv) is the chain rule for the transition x' = Lambda x + b: partial'_a = (partial x^c / partial x'^a) partial_c = (Lambda^{-1})^c_a partial_c; substituting into partial'_a J'^a and using (i) gives the invariance of the divergence, and the (2,0) case follows by the same substitution with the two contravariant factors. (v) An alternating covariant field is a covariant tensor field, so the slot-by-slot covariant law applies; for the volume form, which by def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form is the determinant of the coordinate matrix in an oriented frame, the transformation multiplies the determinant by det(Lambda^{-1}) = 1, and by det Lambda = -1 in the improper case. (vi) is the matrix multiplication of the boost matrix with the component vector; (vii) is the elementary computation J^0 = rho_0 U^0 = rho_0 (U^0/c) c... rather, with u := U/U^0 the identity rho = J^0 = rho_0 U^0 = rho_0 u^0 is immediate, and the last clause is the statement that u^0 = 1 characterizes the charts in which the coordinate density equals the scalar multiplier. The item must not claim that a physical current is a vector field: that adoption belongs to the electromagnetic model, and the final paragraph of the statement records the boundary. All computations are finite algebra and the chain rule for total derivatives.

item.title: A prescribed covariant stress-energy tensor need not be conserved
item.statement: In an inertial chart let $\Omega$ be open and connected and let $F:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$; define the smooth symmetric field $T^{ab}:=F\,\eta^{ab}$. Then $\partial_aT^{ab}=\eta^{ab}\partial_aF=\partial^bF$, so $T$ is conserved on $\Omega$ exactly when $F$ is constant, and for nonconstant $F$ the balance is $\partial_aT^{ab}=\partial^bF$ with nonzero four-force density. Since $\eta$ is constant in every inertial chart, the tensor expression $F\eta$ transforms covariantly under every affine Lorentz map; hence Lorentz covariance of a prescribed tensor expression does not by itself imply conservation, and the balance of an arbitrary prescribed $T$ is an additional premise rather than a consequence of its tensor character. The field $T=F\eta$ is not claimed to be the stress-energy tensor of any of the page's matter models.
item.strategy: Compute $\partial_a(F\eta^{ab})$ using $\partial_a\eta^{ab}=0$ in inertial coordinates; conservation is equivalent to $\partial^bF=0$ for all $b$, i.e. to $F$ constant on the connected domain. The covariance remark follows from [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii) with $\eta'=\eta$. No choice principle is used.

item.title: The flat covariant derivative on affine Minkowski space and fields along curves
item.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space with tangent spaces canonically identified with V, and let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. (a) Vector fields. For smooth vector fields X,Y on Omega (def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space) define the covariant derivative of Y in the direction X at p by (nabla_X Y)(p) := (d/dt)|_{t=0} Y(p + t X(p)); in the inertial chart x of any inertial frame this is (nabla_X Y)^a = X^b partial_b Y^a. The value does not depend on the inertial chart: for another inertial chart x' = Lambda x + b one has partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b and Y'^a = Lambda^a_b Y^b (thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation), and Lambda is constant, so Lambda^a_c X'^b partial'_b Y'^c = X^b partial_b Y^a. nabla_X Y is again a smooth vector field. (b) Covector and general tensor fields. For a smooth covector field alpha set (nabla_X alpha)(Y) := X(alpha(Y)) - alpha(nabla_X Y); for a type (r,s) tensor field T define nabla_X T by the derivation rule on the evaluation of T on smooth vector and covector fields, subtracting nabla_X Y from each vector argument and adding it to each covector argument; in inertial coordinates every component of nabla_X T is X^b partial_b of the component, with no connection coefficients. (c) Properties. nabla is R-bilinear, C^infinity(Omega)-linear in X, satisfies nabla_X(fY) = X(f)Y + f nabla_X Y and the analogous Leibniz rules for tensor fields, is metric compatible (nabla eta = 0, because partial_a eta_{bc} = 0 in every inertial chart), is torsion-free (nabla_X Y - nabla_Y X = [X,Y], def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields and prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket) and has zero curvature (nabla_X nabla_Y Z - nabla_Y nabla_X Z - nabla_{[X,Y]} Z = 0), the last by equality of mixed partial derivatives of the components (thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem). (d) Fields along a curve. If gamma: I -> A is a C^1 curve and W: I -> V is a C^1 field along it (def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve), the covariant derivative of W along gamma is the ordinary V-valued derivative DW/ds := W' (def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral), because the canonical identification T_pA = V is independent of p; consequently parallel transport along any curve is the identity and a field is parallel exactly when it is constant. The derivative (d) is the one used for the acceleration of congruences, for Fermi-Walker transport and for the kinematic decomposition below; the model needs no Christoffel symbols or parallel-transport ODE in this formulation.
item.strategy: Definition with well-definedness obligations. (i) The directional derivative in (a) is the derivative of the V-valued composite t |-> Y(p+tX(p)); its coordinate expression is the chain rule, and chart independence is the displayed finite computation using that inertial transitions are affine (their second derivatives vanish, so no inhomogeneous term appears) and their linear parts are constant. (ii) The extension in (b) is the standard derivation rule on the evaluation of a tensor; the coordinate expression has no Gamma terms because eta is constant and transition matrices are constant in inertial charts. (iii) The properties in (c) are coordinate computations: torsion-freeness is X^b partial_b Y^a - Y^b partial_b X^a = [X,Y]^a, zero curvature is the interchange of mixed partials, and metric compatibility is the constancy of the component matrix eta_{ab}. (iv) In (d), the canonical isomorphism T_pA = V is independent of p, so the covariant derivative along a curve coincides with the ordinary derivative and parallel transport is trivial; this is exactly what makes Fermi-Walker transport below an ordinary linear ODE. No choice principle is used.

item.title: Stress-energy tensor, force density and local balance on flat spacetime
item.statement: Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set. (a) A \emph{stress-energy tensor} on $\Omega$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge1$, is a $C^k$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field $T$ on $\Omega$ in the sense of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]: at every $p$, $T(p):V^*\times V^*\to\mathbb R$ is bilinear and symmetric, so its inertial components satisfy $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)). (b) In the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] with length coordinates $x^0=ct$, the components $T^{ab}$ have the unit joule per cubic metre; the frame components are read as energy density ($T^{00}$), energy flux and momentum density ($T^{0i}=T^{i0}$) and stress ($T^{ij}$). This clause fixes a unit and a reading convention only; it asserts no measurement, no matter model and no dynamics. (c) The \emph{four-force density} of $T$ is the $C^{k-1}$ field with inertial components $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$, where $\partial_a$ are the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. By [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iv) the components $\partial_aT^{ab}$ transform as a vector, so $f$ is a well-defined vector field on $\Omega$, independent of the inertial chart. One says that $T$ is \emph{locally conserved}, or \emph{balanced}, on $\Omega$ when $f=0$ on $\Omega$, and that $T$ is balanced against the four-force density $f$ when $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$. (d) The definition asserts no conservation of any prescribed symmetric field $T$: whether a given $T$ is conserved, whether it arises from an action or a matter model, and whether any of its integrals over a slice converges are separate hypotheses stated elsewhere. No choice principle is used.
item.strategy: Definition item fixing the class of fields, the component readings and the balance terminology. Obligations: (i) $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ is chart-independent because $T$ is a symmetric bilinear form and the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii) is linear in the tensor; (ii) $\partial_aT^{ab}$ is a $(1,0)$-component family under an affine change of inertial chart by clause (iv) of the same theorem, since the transition matrix is constant; (iii) the unit statement is a convention imported from [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] extended to the density components, and carries no mathematical content; (iv) no positivity, symmetry of the integral representation, conservation or dynamics is asserted. No choice principle is used.

item.title: Dust stress-energy in a boosted inertial frame
item.statement: In an inertial frame $x$ let dust at rest have rest energy density $\rho>0$, so $T^{ab}=\rho\,\delta^a_0\delta^b_0$; the only nonzero component is $T^{00}=\rho$. Consider the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along the $x^1$ axis with parameter $\beta$, $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$: $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$, $x'^2=x^2$, $x'^3=x^3$. By the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii), $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2\beta\rho,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2\beta^2\rho,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=0,$$ all remaining components zero; equivalently $T'=\rho\,n'\otimes n'$ where $n'$ is the image of $e_0$ under the boost, $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$, the future unit direction of the dust in the primed frame. The primed energy density $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho$ carries one factor of $\gamma$ from the increased energy of each dust particle and one from the contracted volume, as in the source computation. All primed components are constant, so $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=0$, consistently with [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. The example is a component computation; it asserts no measurement and no dynamics.
item.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$ with the boost matrix $\Lambda$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: only $T^{00}=\rho$ contributes, giving the displayed components; the identification $T'=\rho n'\otimes n'$ follows from $n'=\Lambda e_0$. Constancy and conservation are immediate. Source: Crowell Example 5 p. 185 and (1.106) of Carroll. No choice principle is used.

item.title: Worked current boost law and coordinate versus rest density
item.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial frame with coordinates (x^0,x^1) consider the constant future unit vector field U with components (U^0,U^1) = (5/4,3/4), so eta_0(U,U) = -25/16 + 9/16 = -1, and a constant scalar rho_0; put J := rho_0 U. Then: (i) J has components (J^0,J^1) = (5rho_0/4, 3rho_0/4) and partial_a J^a = 0 because the components are constant, so the continuity equation of thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation(vi) holds and reads partial_0 J^0 + partial_1 J^1 = 0 identically. (ii) Under the passive boost B = B((3/5)e_1) one computes B U = e_0: BU has first component (5/4)(5/4 - (3/5)(3/4)) = (5/4)(16/20) = 1 and second component (5/4)(3/4 - (3/5)(5/4)) = (5/4)(0) = 0. Correspondingly B J = (rho_0,0), the components of rho_0 U in the chart in which U = e_0. Hence the coordinate density J^0 is 5rho_0/4 in the original chart and rho_0 in the rest chart, while the scalar multiplier rho_0 is the same; this is the worked instance of thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation(vii). (iii) The general boost law of clause (vi) reproduces (ii): J'^0 = gamma(J^0 - beta J^1) = (5/4)(5rho_0/4 - (3/5)(3rho_0/4)) = (5/4)(16rho_0/20) = rho_0 and J'^1 = gamma(J^1 - beta J^0) = (5/4)(3rho_0/4 - (3/5)(5rho_0/4)) = 0. The example carries no physical charge assignment: it illustrates the transformation of a specified vector field, and the identification of J with a physical current is a model premise of the electromagnetic framework.
item.strategy: All clauses are exact rational evaluations of the boost matrix on the displayed components; clause (ii) is the direct substitution of U into the boost formula, and clause (iii) is the boost law of thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation(vi). The distinction between the scalar rho_0 and the coordinate density J^0 in the two charts is the point of clause (vii) of that theorem.

item.title: A passive boost that brings a moving particle to rest
item.statement: In the setting of [[ex-sr-four-momentum-at-beta-three-fifths]], let $B(\beta)$ be the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] with parameter $\beta=3/5$ along $e_1$, and let $P'$ be the components of $P$ after the coordinate change $x'=B(\beta)x$ with $v=3c/5$. Then $P'=(mc,0,0,0)$: the energy becomes $E'=mc^2$ and the spatial momentum vanishes, and the mass shell gives $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=m^2c^4$. The observer energy of the same particle thus changes from $5mc^2/4$ to $mc^2$ while the invariant mass stays $m$; in particular $T_{e'_0}(P)=0$ in the new frame, the frame of the particle's rest.
item.strategy: Substitute $\gamma_v=5/4$, $E=5mc^2/4$, $p_\parallel=3mc/4$ into the boost transformation of [[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]]\,(c): $E'=\gamma_v(E-vp_\parallel)=5/4\,(5mc^2/4-9mc^2/20)=mc^2$ and $p'_\parallel=\gamma_v(p_\parallel-vE/c^2)=0$. Check the mass shell and read the rest-frame property from [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(b).

item.title: Perfect fluid components in its rest frame and in a moving frame
item.statement: Let $T^{ab}=(\varepsilon+P)n^an^b+P\eta^{ab}$ be the perfect-fluid tensor of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]], with $n$ future unit. In an inertial frame with $n=e_0$ (fluid at rest) the components are $T^{00}=\varepsilon$, $T^{11}=T^{22}=T^{33}=P$ and all other components zero. Under the passive boost along $x^1$ with parameter $\beta$ (so that in the primed frame the fluid moves with speed $v=\beta c$ in the negative $x'^1$ direction), the component law gives $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)\beta^2+P,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=P,$$ all remaining components zero. In particular the observer at rest in the primed frame measures the energy density $T'(e_0',e_0')=T'^{00}=\gamma^2(\varepsilon+P)-P$, which differs from the rest-frame density $\varepsilon$ unless $\beta=0$ and is at least $\varepsilon$ when $\varepsilon+P\ge0$; the transverse diagonal components stay equal to the pressure $P$. The computation uses the observer decomposition of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] to read $T'^{00}$ as an energy density; it asserts no equation of state and no measurement.
item.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_d[(\varepsilon+P)n^cn^d+P\eta^{cd}]$ using $\eta'=\eta$ (metric preservation, [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]]) and $n'=\Lambda n$ with $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$; the displayed components follow. The energy-density reading is clause (c) of [[lem-sr-observer-stress-energy-decomposition]] at $n=e_0'$. Source: (4.53) of Tong, (1.107)-(1.110) of Carroll and 9.2.6 of Crowell. No choice principle is used.

item.title: Worked covector and vector component transformation under a beta = 3/5 boost
item.statement: Worked computation. In an inertial frame with coordinates (x^0,x^1) and the passive boost Lambda = B((3/5)e_1), so Lambda = [[5/4,-3/4],[-3/4,5/4]] and Lambda^{-1} = B((-3/5)e_1) = [[5/4,3/4],[3/4,5/4]] (def-lorentz-boost, thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation). Take the covector k with components (k_0,k_1) = (-1,1) and the vector w with components (w^0,w^1) = (1,1). Then: (i) k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b gives k'_0 = (5/4)(-1) + (3/4)(1) = -1/2 and k'_1 = (3/4)(-1) + (5/4)(1) = 1/2, so k' = (-1/2,1/2). (ii) w'^a = Lambda^a_b w^b gives w'^0 = (5/4)(1 - 3/5) = 1/2 and w'^1 = (5/4)(1 - 3/5) = 1/2, so w' = (1/2,1/2). (iii) Both k and w are null in eta_0: -1 + 1 = 0, and so are k' and w': -1/4 + 1/4 = 0. (iv) The contraction is invariant: k'_a w'^a = (-1/2)(1/2) + (1/2)(1/2) = 0 = (-1)(1) + (1)(1) = k_a w^a. The example shows all three features of the component law: the covariant slot transforms with Lambda^{-1}, the contravariant slot with Lambda, and the contraction is unchanged; the common factor 1/2 on the null covector is the numerical form of the transformation law and no frequency or Doppler interpretation is attached to it here (that belongs to the light-and-doppler page).
item.strategy: Every entry is an exact rational matrix-vector computation from the displayed matrices Lambda and Lambda^{-1}. The transformation laws applied are clauses (i) and (ii) of thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation; the nullness and contraction checks are direct evaluations of eta_0 and of the component pairing.

item.title: Four-momentum components, energy-velocity relation and passive boost transformation in an inertial frame
item.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with stationary observer $n:=e_0$; let $E_n,q_n$ be as in [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].
(a) For every $P\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ the coordinate components of $P$ in the frame are $(P^0,P^1,P^2,P^3)=(E_n(P)/c,\,q^1,q^2,q^3)$, where $q_n(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3q^ie_i$; if $P$ is future timelike then $E^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2\sum_{i=1}^3(q^i)^2$ with $E=E_n(P)$.
(b) Let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^1$ future timelike worldline whose chart coordinate path is $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$, with coordinate velocity $w:=r'$ and $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$; then $|w|<c$, the four-velocity is $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e), and for $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant the components are $P=m\gamma_w(c,w)$, that is $E_n(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $q_n(P)=\sum_{i=1}^3m\gamma_ww^ie_i$.
(c) Let $B(\beta)$ be the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] with parameter $\beta=v/c$, $|v|<c$, along a spatial direction $s$, and let $P'$ denote the components of the same vector $P$ after the coordinate change $x'=B(\beta)x$; write $\mathbf p=(P^1,P^2,P^3)$ and split it into its components $\mathbf p_\parallel$, $\mathbf p_\perp$ with respect to $s$. Then
$$P'^0=\gamma_v\bigl(P^0-\beta\,s\cdot\mathbf p\bigr),\qquad \mathbf p'_\parallel=\gamma_v\bigl(\mathbf p_\parallel-\beta P^0\bigr),\qquad \mathbf p'_\perp=\mathbf p_\perp,$$
equivalently $E'=\gamma_v(E-v\,p_\parallel)$, $p'_\parallel=\gamma_v(p_\parallel-vE/c^2)$, $p'_\perp=p_\perp$. The quadratic combination is invariant, $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike $P$, while for future null $P$ one has $E=c|\mathbf p|$ and $E'=c|\mathbf p'|$ in both coordinate systems; in particular the invariant mass is frame-independent.
item.strategy: (a) The decomposition $P=(E_n/c)e_0+q_n(P)$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] is already a decomposition in the basis; read components and substitute the mass-shell identity of [[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)(ii). (b) [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e) gives $|w|<c$ and $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$; multiply by $m$ and apply (a). (c) $P$ is a vector; the component law $v'^a=L^a{}_bv^b$ under the coordinate change $x'=Lx+b$ is [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]], and the matrix of $B(\beta)$ in the frame basis is displayed in [[def-lorentz-boost]] ($B^0{}_0=\gamma_v$, $B^0{}_i=B^i{}_0=-\gamma_v\beta s_i$, $B^i{}_j=\delta^i_j+(\gamma_v-1)s_is_j$); reading off the rows gives the displayed components, and [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]] shows the transformed frame is inertial. The invariance is the rearrangement $E'^2-c^2|\mathbf p'|^2=E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2$ of the same components, equal to $-c^2\eta(P,P)=m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike $P$ and to $0$ for future null $P$ ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a)). No choice principle is used.

item.title: Transformation of the frame data of a future null wave covector under a passive boost
item.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is x' = B(beta) x + b for some beta in R^3 with |beta| < 1 and some b in R^4, where B(beta) is the passive boost of def-lorentz-boost and gamma := (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2), and let k be a future null wave covector with frame-x data (varpi,s) as in lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data, so that k has components (k_0,k_1,k_2,k_3) = (-varpi, varpi s_1, varpi s_2, varpi s_3) in x. Then: (i) the components of the same covector k in x' are k'_a = (B(-beta))^b_a k_b, that is k'_0 = gamma(k_0 + beta . k_vec) and k'_vec = k_vec + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . k_vec) beta + gamma beta k_0 for beta nonzero (and k' = k for beta = 0), where k_vec := (k_1,k_2,k_3). (ii) With varpi' := -k'_0 and s'_i := k'_i/varpi' the frame-x' data is varpi' = gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi > 0 and s' = [s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s) beta - gamma beta] / [gamma(1 - beta . s)] for beta nonzero (and s' = s for beta = 0); moreover |s'| = 1, so k'_a = (-varpi', varpi' s'_1, varpi' s'_2, varpi' s'_3) in x'. (iii) In the axis case beta = b e_1 with b in (-1,1): s'_1 = (s_1 - b)/(1 - b s_1), s'_2 = s_2/(gamma(1 - b s_1)) and s'_3 = s_3/(gamma(1 - b s_1)). (iv) beta . s' = (beta . s - |beta|^2)/(1 - beta . s); in particular beta . s' = 0 if and only if beta . s = |beta|^2, and beta . s' = -|beta|^2 if and only if beta . s = 0. (v) applying the transformation with beta replaced by -beta returns the original data (varpi,s), since B(-beta) is the inverse of B(beta). The statement is pure algebra of eta and the boost; no choice principle is used.
item.strategy: Proof strategy. (i) The transition x' = B(beta)x + b has linear part Lambda = B(beta), which is a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix representing the inertial frame change (lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz, def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group); the covector component law k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b is clause (ii) of thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation (for the constant covector field k, of class C^infinity in the sense of def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space). By lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, Lambda^{-1} has entries (B(-beta))^0_0 = gamma, (B(-beta))^0_i = (B(-beta))^i_0 = gamma beta_i and (B(-beta))^i_j = delta^i_j + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) beta_i beta_j (for beta nonzero), which gives the displayed component formulas. (ii) Insert k_0 = -varpi and k_i = varpi s_i: k'_0 = gamma(-varpi + varpi beta . s) = -gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi, so varpi' = gamma(1 - beta . s) varpi; positivity follows from |beta| < 1 and |s| = 1 via the Cauchy-Schwarz bound beta . s <= |beta| < 1 (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite), so 1 - beta . s >= 1 - |beta| > 0. The numerator for k'_vec is k_vec + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . k_vec) beta + gamma beta k_0 = varpi[s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s) beta - gamma beta], so dividing by varpi' gives the displayed s'. Finally |s'| = 1 is not assumed but follows from part (b) of lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data applied in the inertial frame x': the same covector k is future null (k^sharp is unchanged by a change of frame; only its components change), and the lemma's construction in x' returns precisely (varpi', s') as computed. (iii) Substituting beta = b e_1 and |beta|^2 = b^2 gives s'_1 = (s_1 - b)/(1 - b s_1) and s'_j = s_j/(gamma(1 - b s_1)) for j = 2,3. (iv) beta . s' = [beta . s + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . s)|beta|^2 - gamma|beta|^2]/[gamma(1 - beta . s)] = [gamma(beta . s) - gamma|beta|^2]/[gamma(1 - beta . s)] = (beta . s - |beta|^2)/(1 - beta . s); the two equivalences follow since |beta| < 1. (v) By lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse B(-beta) is the inverse of B(beta), so applying the component law twice returns k'' = k; equivalently substituting -beta in (ii) inverts the explicit formulas. Scope note: pure algebra; the item asserts no physical Doppler statement (that is pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration) and no choice principle is used.

item.title: Hodge reconstruction of an alternating two-tensor and the optional SI field split
item.statement: Let $(V,\eta)$ be the oriented Lorentz vector space of the affine Minkowski model with orientation and volume form $\varepsilon$ of [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], and let $F:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ be an alternating bilinear form ([[def-alternating-k-linear-map]], [[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]]). Define the Hodge dual by $(*F)_{ab}:=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ and set $(\alpha\wedge\beta)_{ab}:=\alpha_a\beta_b-\alpha_b\beta_a$. Let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and put $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$. (a) $e(n)=b(n)=0$, and $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ with $n^\flat:=\eta(n,\cdot)$; also $*(*F)=-F$, so the Hodge dual squares to $-1$ on two-forms. (b) In an oriented orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$: $e_i=F_{i0}$, $b_i=-\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$, $F_{0i}=-e_i$ and $F_{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$; hence the six components of $F$ are exactly the six components of the pair $(e,b)$ and the reconstruction in (a) is equivalent to these component formulae. (c) The quadratic invariants are $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4\,(e\cdot b)$, where $|\cdot|$ and $\cdot$ are those of the spatial structure of the frame ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]); the two combinations are the independent quadratic invariants of $F$. (d) (Optional SI identification.) If in an inertial frame one identifies $F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ for spatial vector fields $E,B$, then $e_i=-E_i/c$ and $b_i=B_i$, the invariants of (c) read $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,(E\cdot B)/c$, and under the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along $e_1$ with parameter $\beta$ one has $E'_1=E_1$, $B'_1=B_1$, $E'_\perp=\gamma(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$ with $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v=\beta c$ along $e_1$. (e) The theorem is algebra on the oriented Lorentz vector space with the stated index and duality conventions; clause (d) is an explicitly optional identification of the components of $F$ with fields the electromagnetic framework names $E,B$, and the theorem asserts no field equation, no dynamics, no measurement and no transformation beyond the stated component law. No choice principle is used.
item.strategy: Work in the oriented orthonormal frame with $n=e_0$ ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)): write $F_{0i}=-e_i$ (this defines $e_i$ through $F_{i0}$), and the spatial block determines a three-vector $b$ by $F_{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$; antisymmetry fixes all components. Evaluate $(*F)_{ab}=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ab}{}^{cd}F_{cd}$ componentwise using $\varepsilon^{0123}=-1$ ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]) to obtain $b_i=-\tfrac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}$ and the reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$; verify $*^2=-1$ on the six basis bivectors by direct evaluation. The invariant formulas follow by expanding in this frame; the boost law follows from the tensor component law [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii) applied to $F$ under the passive boost $\Lambda$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]] ([[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]]), substituting the SI identifications. Sources: the tensor component law and the Hodge-star algebra are the flat restriction of S8 of the research supplier argument; the duality conventions and the field-strength components are documented in Carroll Chapter 1 pp. 16-24 and Tong 4.5.1. No choice principle is used.
